claims.text: An MLIP trained on ab initio liquid snapshots of equimolar NiCoFeCrMn will improve reference–target phase-space overlap relative to a standard EAM reference.
Using the MLIP as the thermodynamic-integration reference will reduce path mismatch relative to TOR-TILD using standard EAM references.
The proposed system is liquid equimolar Ni-Co-Fe-Cr-Mn at temperatures from Tm to Tm+200 K.
The MLIP will represent local coordination environments more accurately than EAM.
The MLIP will represent ab initio force distributions more accurately than EAM.
More faithful reproduction of ab initio forces and liquid structure will make the MLIP ensemble sample configurations more representative of the ab initio liquid.
Sampling configurations more representative of the ab initio liquid will increase reference–target phase-space overlap.
Increased reference–target overlap will lower thermodynamic-integration barriers or path mismatch.
The MLIP reference is predicted to reduce thermodynamic-integration path mismatch by approximately 30–50% compared with standard EAM references.
The proposed applicability range is multicomponent HEA liquids near melting.
The method has not been validated for solid phases or single-component liquids.
Performance is untested for alloys with more than five components or non-equimolar compositions.
Failure to obtain at least a 20% mismatch reduction at both Tm and Tm+100 K would falsify the hypothesis.
